sections.title: R7 router troubleshooting guide
sections.text: Skylink R7 Router - Tier 1 Troubleshooting Guide Support Knowledge Article KA-0412, version 6. Applies to R7 firmware 2.8 and later.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.text: This guide helps Tier 1 support agents resolve the most common Skylink R7 router issues on the first contact. Follow the sections in order unless the customer's symptom clearly matches a specific issue in Section 4. Before starting, collect the router serial number (on the label under the device), the firmware version (Admin Console > System) and the customer's ISP. Log all three in the ticket.
sections.summary: Explains that this guide is for Tier 1 agents handling Skylink R7 router tickets and lists what to collect before troubleshooting.

sections.title: 2 LED Status Reference
sections.text: The front panel LEDs are the fastest way to narrow down a problem. Ask the customer to describe the color and whether each light is solid or blinking. Figure 1: R7 front panel with an amber INTERNET indicator LED Solid green Blinking green Amber Off POWER Normal Booting / updating Hardware fault No power INTERNET Online Traffic WAN up, no IP from ISP No WAN cable 2.4G / 5G Radio on Traffic Radio error Radio disabled LAN Device connected Traffic - No device WPS Paired Pairing (2 min) Pairing failed Idle
sections.summary: Shows the front panel LEDs and explains what each color and blink pattern means.

sections.title: 3 Diagnostic Flow
sections.text: Use this flow for any 'no internet' contact. It resolves about 64% of these tickets without escalation. Figure 2: No-internet diagnostic flowchart When closing a ticket, always use the resolution code shown in the flowchart so that reporting stays accurate.
sections.summary: Presents the no-internet decision flowchart that routes agents from power checks to reboot to Tier 2 escalation.

sections.title: 4.1 No Internet
sections.text: 1. Confirm whether all devices or only one device is affected. 2. Check the INTERNET LED. If off, reseat the WAN cable at both ends. 3. Power-cycle the modem first, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the router. 4. If the INTERNET LED stays amber, ask the customer to contact their ISP to confirm there is no outage. 5. If still unresolved, collect WAN logs (Admin Console > Diagnostics > Export) and escalate.
sections.summary: Gives step-by-step checks for a customer with no internet connection, including power cycling and verifying the WAN cable.

sections.title: 4.2 Slow Wi-Fi
sections.text: Ask the customer to run a speed test next to the router, then in the problem room. Recommend the 5 GHz network for devices within two rooms of the router. Move the router off the floor and away from microwaves and fish tanks. Enable Auto Channel (Wireless > Advanced) to avoid congested channels. Confirm firmware is 2.9.1 or later, which fixes a 5 GHz throughput issue.
sections.summary: Lists causes of slow Wi-Fi such as band choice, placement, channel congestion and outdated firmware.

sections.title: 4.3 Firmware Update Failure
sections.text: Error E-217 means the downloaded firmware image did not pass its checksum check, usually because the download was interrupted. The router keeps running the old firmware, so it is safe. Figure 3: Admin Console showing firmware update error E-217 Ask the customer to click Retry download. If it fails twice, send them the direct download link from KA-0388 and walk them through Upload file manually. Do not ask customers to factory reset for this error.
sections.summary: Explains error E-217 (checksum mismatch after download) and how to retry or upload the firmware manually.

sections.title: 5 Escalation
sections.text: Escalate only after completing the relevant steps above and attaching logs. Tickets escalated without logs will be returned. Condition Escalate to Target response No internet after full diagnostic flow Tier 2 Network 4 business hours POWER LED amber (hardware fault) RMA team 1 business day E-217 after manual upload Tier 2 Firmware 4 business hours Suspected security issue (unknown admin login) Security on-call 1 hour, 24/7 More than 20 tickets with same symptom in 1 hour Incident manager 15 minutes
sections.summary: Defines when and how to escalate to Tier 2 or Engineering, with response-time targets.

sections.title: Q3 2026 support review
sections.text: Q3 2026 Customer Support Review Prepared by Support Operations for the leadership review on 6 October 2026.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.text: Q3 was a strong quarter for customer satisfaction and speed of response, but the R7 firmware 2.9.0 rollout in weeks 33 and 34 created a spike in contacts that we have not fully recovered from. Backlog older than 7 days grew 19% and is the main risk heading into Q4.
sections.summary: Summarizes Q3: 12,480 tickets resolved, CSAT up to 91.3%, faster first response, but a growing backlog after the R7 2.9.0 rollout.

sections.title: Key Metrics
sections.text: Figure 1: Support KPI dashboard for Q3 2026 Metric Q2 2026 Q3 2026 Target Status Tickets resolved 11,556 12,480 - - CSAT 89.2% 91.3% 90% On track First response time (median) 2h 51m 2h 14m 2h 30m On track First contact resolution 58% 61% 65% Behind Backlog > 7 days 180 214 < 150 At risk
sections.summary: Shows the KPI dashboard and a table comparing Q2 and Q3 values against targets.

sections.title: Ticket Volume
sections.text: Weekly volume rose from 870 tickets at the start of the quarter to a peak of 1,260 in week 34, when R7 firmware 2.9.0 was rolled out to all customers. Most of the extra contacts were about failed updates (error E-217) and a 5 GHz speed regression, both fixed in 2.9.1. Figure 2: Weekly new tickets in Q3 2026
sections.summary: Describes weekly ticket volume through Q3, with a peak of 1,260 tickets in week 34 due to the R7 2.9.0 rollout.

sections.title: Top Contact Drivers
sections.text: Rank Contact reason Tickets Share Change vs Q2 1 No internet 3,120 25% -3% 2 Firmware update failure (E-217) 1,870 15% +212% 3 Slow Wi-Fi 1,560 12.5% +18% 4 Account and billing 1,310 10.5% -6% 5 Setup and installation 1,190 9.5% +2%
sections.summary: Ranks the five largest contact reasons, led by no-internet issues and firmware update failures.

sections.title: Customer Feedback
sections.text: We analyzed 3,904 CSAT survey comments. Positive comments most often mention agent friendliness and quick fixes. Negative comments cluster around the firmware update issue and having to explain the problem again after escalation. "Agent fixed my internet in five minutes and explained what went wrong." "Third time contacting you about the same update error." "I had to repeat everything when I was transferred to Tier 2."
sections.summary: Highlights themes from CSAT comments: praise for fast agents, frustration with firmware issues and repeated contacts.

sections.title: Q4 Priorities
sections.text: 1. Reduce backlog older than 7 days to under 150 by 15 November with a dedicated backlog squad. 2. Introduce warm handoffs to Tier 2 so customers do not have to repeat themselves. 3. Publish an in-app guide for E-217 to deflect an estimated 40% of update-failure contacts. 4. Hire 6 seasonal agents for the holiday peak starting 1 December.
sections.summary: Lists four Q4 priorities: backlog reduction, warm handoffs to Tier 2, update-failure deflection and holiday staffing.

sections.title: Skylink limited warranty
sections.text: Skylink Hardware Limited Warranty Applies to products purchased in the United States and Canada on or after 1 March 2026.

sections.title: 1 What This Warranty Covers
sections.text: Skylink Networks Inc. ("Skylink") warrants that its hardware products will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use during the warranty period. If a defect arises, Skylink will, at its option, repair the product, replace it with a new or refurbished product of equal or better functionality, or refund the purchase price. This warranty applies only to the original purchaser and only to products purchased from Skylink or an authorized reseller. Proof of purchase is required.
sections.summary: States that Skylink warrants hardware against defects in materials and workmanship under normal use.

sections.title: 2 Warranty Period
sections.text: Product Warranty period Extended option R7 and R9 routers 3 years Skylink Care+ extends to 5 years M3 mesh nodes 2 years Skylink Care+ extends to 4 years Power adapters and cables 1 year Not available Refurbished products 1 year Not available
sections.summary: Gives the warranty period by product line, from 1 year for accessories to 3 years for routers.

sections.title: 3 What Is Not Covered
sections.text: Damage caused by accidents, liquid, fire, lightning or power surges. Products that have been opened, modified or repaired by anyone other than Skylink. Use of third-party or custom firmware. Cosmetic damage and normal wear and tear. Products with a removed or altered serial number. Loss of data or configuration settings.
sections.summary: Lists exclusions such as accidental damage, unauthorized modification, normal wear and third-party firmware.

sections.title: 4 How to Make a Claim
sections.text: 1. Contact Skylink Support at support.skylink.example or 1-800-555-0142. 2. Complete troubleshooting with an agent to confirm a hardware defect. 3. Receive a Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) number by email. 4. Ship the product with the RMA number to the address provided. Skylink pays return shipping for valid claims. 5. Replacement products ship within 5 business days of receipt. Customers with Skylink Care+ receive advance replacement: a replacement ships before the defective unit is returned.
sections.summary: Explains the steps to file a warranty claim through the support portal and ship the product for RMA.

sections.title: 5 Limitation of Liability
sections.text: To the maximum extent permitted by law, Skylink is not liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, including loss of data, revenue or profits, arising from the use of or inability to use the product. Skylink's total liability is limited to the amount paid for the product. Some jurisdictions do not allow these limitations, so they may not apply to you. This warranty gives you specific legal rights, and you may have other rights that vary by state or province.
sections.summary: Limits Skylink's liability to the purchase price and excludes indirect damages where permitted by law.
